title: Tactical Empathy
description: Understanding and naming the other side's position out loud, before you push your own.

sections.title: Quick Understanding
sections.content: Tactical empathy is the deliberate practice of recognising and voicing what the other person is feeling and why. Naming their position accurately makes them feel understood — and people who feel understood become far easier to move.

sections.title: Why It Works
sections.content: Being understood reduces threat and defensiveness. Once the other side feels heard, they stop repeating their position and start listening, which opens room for agreement.

sections.title: Real-Life Examples
content: "It sounds like the deadline is putting you under real pressure."
"It seems like you're worried this sets a precedent you'll have to live with."

sections.title: What It Looks Like
content: A negotiator who describes the other side's position before their own.
Statements that show you understand, not that you agree.

sections.title: How to Use It
sections.content: Listen for the emotion and the reason behind it. Say it back plainly and calmly. Do not attach a demand to it — the naming alone does the work.

sections.title: Red Flags
content: Empathy used as a script to manipulate rather than to understand.
Naming a feeling you have not actually listened for.

sections.title: Defense Strategies
content: Notice when your position is being summarised back to you unusually well.
Being understood does not oblige you to concede anything.

sections.title: Key Lessons
content: Name their position before pressing yours.
Empathy is a tool, not a concession.
